mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES stays near -39% while TRANSIT stays near -30%, weekday downtown trip density remains depressed and retail-and-recreation mobility falls further over the next four weeks because fewer commuters generate fewer incidental retail visits.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not decline relative to the prior four-week mean despite WORKPLACES remaining below -35% and TRANSIT below -28% for the next month.

mechanism_narrative: A week-on-week rise in PARKS to above 12% indicates a shift toward outdoor discretionary time, which diverts time and spending away from enclosed retail venues and lowers RETAIL_REC over the following two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS crosses above 12% and remains there for at least one weekly mean
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 14 days after PARKS exceeds 12% in weekly mean values.

mechanism_narrative: When GROCERY_PHARM is elevated while RESIDENTIAL is also elevated, households compress errands into local-neighborhood trips and substitute away from shopping districts, producing a modest rise in RETAIL_REC within one week.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM stays above -25% and RESIDENTIAL stays above 5%
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not improve within 7 days when GROCERY_PHARM remains above -25% and RESIDENTIAL remains above 5%.

mechanism_narrative: A recovery in TRANSIT toward -25% or better marks easing access to Manhattan retail corridors; once that threshold is crossed, retail visitation should improve over the next four weeks as trip friction falls.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC stays flat or declines over the next 28 days after TRANSIT improves to better than -25% weekly mean.

mechanism_narrative: If PARKS strengthens while WORKPLACES remains deeply negative, discretionary nonwork time crowds out shopping trips and retail mobility falls over the next four weeks; the signal is strongest when park activity is above 10% and workplaces stay below -35%.
candidate_trigger: PARKS above 10% while WORKPLACES stays below -35%
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases over the next month despite PARKS above 10% and WORKPLACES below -35% throughout the period.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained summer pattern of rising PARKS and stable RESIDENTIAL implies more local leisure and neighborhood time, which should support retail and recreation mobility after a short lag as people combine outings with shopping.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to rise over the next 14 days while PARKS remains elevated and RESIDENTIAL remains above baseline.

mechanism_narrative: If TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both improve together, commuting-based foot traffic returns to Manhattan retail nodes and RETAIL_REC rises over the next four weeks; isolated movement in only one series should not be enough to shift retail mobility materially.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT improves by at least 3 points and WORKPLACES improves by at least 3 points within the same week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase over 28 days after simultaneous weekly improvements in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES.

mechanism_narrative: When GROCERY_PHARM remains less depressed than retail and WORKPLACES stays near its current trough, errand concentration in local mixed-use areas substitutes for central shopping trips and keeps RETAIL_REC below its last-four-week average over the next month.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM is at least 10 points above WORKPLACES
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises relative to the prior four-week mean even though GROCERY_PHARM stays at least 10 points above WORKPLACES for the full horizon.
